lines.text: Garrow and Kell led us straight into the White. Trees of ice. Snow to the waist. And around my feet, as always, a path of melting slush I couldn't have stopped if I'd tried.
Walk in his footprints, Wren. The ice under the snow is thin here.
I know how to walk on ice, Father.
It was the first time I had ever heard her call him that.
Look at them. Strolling along like it's a summer road. In my day, peasants carried the baggage and kept their mouths shut.
In your day, my lord, did the peasants carry you too?
Shut up, boy.
And remind me why we're dragging Tobin's Mistake through a blizzard?
It's not a mistake! It killed a wyrm! And it's just in case!
On the second morning, the hillside above Halvard's riders gave way.
Bren! Osric! Dig, damn you! Dig!
My farmers were already digging. They threw blocks of snow aside like bales of hay. Tobin pulled a horse out by its saddle, with the rider still on it.
Got one! Is he yours, my lord? He's very cold. You can have him back.
Twelve men and ten horses went into that drift. Every one of them came out alive. Halvard counted them twice.
Your farmers.
Greyhollow.
Does this mean we're friends now? I'm very easy to be friends with.
Drink, boy. Before I change my mind.
At dusk on the second day, we came over the last ridge and saw Kesting.
A black keep on a crag, its walls lined with torches. And all around it, filling the pass like a white sea, the beasts of the Pale.
Still standing. Good lads. Good lads.
And behind the keep, in the falling snow, something very large opened its eyes.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-four, coming soon.
